instruments_this_issue: analysis/weather_newcomer.py - pooled-window newcomer refresh cells, issue #6's pre-registered replacement for a second consecutive dark per-issue cell. Also now the single source for the per-issue cell construction, which weather_gpu.py imports rather than duplicates.

analysis/weather_lemmy_ref.py coverage_bound() - bounds the same parse bias on the frozen comparator from its published n_classified, so the correction can be assessed on both sides without re-measuring the frozen corpus.

analysis/weather_trend_tests.py - the two significance figures the prose cites (the allocation sign-count tail and the dip-rate Fisher test), read out of the published results.json so they cannot drift from what shipped. analysis/weather_dip_rate.py - the shared-prefix assertion now reports WHICH windows moved, by how much, and whether any crossed the forth anchor. It fired for the first time this issue; a bare 'VIOLATED' would not have said whether the published dip counts survived.

idea_time_series.halves_note: the halves split the WHOLE series, so consecutive issues' second halves cover overlapping but different window sets and the statistic lags the current level; demoted in issue #6 and kept only because, unlike the retired running means, it does move with new windows. The cross-issue second-half series is #2 0.1343 -> #3 0.1323 -> #4 0.1324 -> #5 0.1298 -> #6 0.1295 -> #7 0.1295 - unchanged to four decimals, so issue #6's record low was matched, not extended. The pull-1 figure 0.1348 is a WHOLE-series mean and does not belong in that sequence.
idea_time_series.dip_rate_note: per-issue rate over the windows each issue actually added: 10.3 -> 15.6 -> 30.8 -> 32.0 -> 47.6 -> 42.1 -> 10.5%. THE SERIES MIXES WINDOW KINDS: #5's 63 windows came from a THREE-DAY issue window, #6's 19 and #7's 19 from ONE-DAY windows, so the only like-kind comparison at the tail is #7 vs #6 - which is the pair weather_trend_tests.py tests. Issue #6 set the trigger: a third issue in the 40s would make 'roughly half of all windows dip below the nearest anchor' a standing reading. It did NOT happen - the rate fell to its lowest since issue #2 (a ranking that spans both kinds), and the new-window mean rose to 0.1335 (#6 0.1299, #5 0.1276). 2/19 against 8/19 is Fisher two-sided p = 0.0625, and the 120-item windows advance by 40 so each issue's 19 windows carry roughly 6-7 independent observations, making Fisher on the nominal n anti-conservative - a test that already fails to reach significance fails a fortiori. DIRECTION clear, change NOT distinguishable. The pooled column fell for the first time (23.9 -> 23.1%), which is composition.

prefix_drift_this_issue.cause: post:1197, a post-publication edit on 08-18 20:38:08 that cut the item from 2384 to 246 chars (feed_lag.content_mutations). weather_gpu.py evicted its cached claim and re-claimified it; the 3 moved windows are exactly the 3 that contain it (W=120, stride 40). activity_clock_signatures.design: each corpus's first min(N, n_agent) items split into 7 equal item-count windows; core = active in >=3 windows; clock-free, commensurable by construction

structure.churn_control_note: dominance and stability survive the fixed-span control; core_n was retired in issue #5 and the fixed-span PERMEABILITY row is retired as a cross-issue series THIS issue. The reason is REASSIGNMENT, not turnover: the populations barely change (the 5-day cell's eligible cohorts hold 180 authors at #6 and 161 at #7, sharing 152 - Jaccard 0.80, and 0.92 at the 7-day span), but an author's 'first window' is re-derived relative to the span, so the same people are sorted into different cohorts as the span slides - #6's 130-author '08-14' cohort is largely #7's 123-author '08-15' cohort. The cell re-partitions a stable population every issue, which is the composition defect the fixed-horizon running mean was retired for. The row is still emitted (7d 43.7 -> 52.2, 5d 47.3 -> 54.6) and is NOT read. Dominance and stability are span-level, not cohort-level. This issue the controlled dominance widths DISAGREE for a second consecutive issue: 7-day 91.8 -> 91.7 (-0.1) against 5-day 88.4 -> 91.0 (+2.6), so under issue #6's own rule neither 'still rising' nor 'plateaued near 92%' is available. Controlled stability fell at both widths (7d 1.25 -> 1.19, 5d 1.32 -> 1.25), so issue #6's first-non-decline did not persist.
structure.permeability_note: The published day-window average rose 43.9 -> 46.9 on an IDENTICAL ten-cohort set for the SECOND consecutive issue (#5, #6 and #7 all draw on 08-06..08-15; issue #4's cell drew on seven cohorts, so #4->#5 was not membership-fixed), so with membership constant that movement can only be observation length. The fixed-horizon cells behaved as the retirement predicts: per-cohort identity HOLDS at all three horizons, and N=3 and N=4 are BIT-IDENTICAL to issue #6 (32.2 and 37.6). N=5 moved 38.3 -> 41.7 purely because the 08-15 cohort's window closed and it entered at 72.7% (n=11); over the shared 9 cohorts it reads 38.3. UNDISCLOSED FLOOR, now disclosed: weather_permeability_control.py counts a cohort only at n>=10, so 08-16 (n=7, 14.3% at N=3) and 08-17 (n=6, 50.0%) DID complete their N=3 windows this issue and were dropped, as 08-05 (n=6) has been throughout. 'No cohort entered' is the floor, not the calendar. Sensitivity: at a n>=5 floor N=3 gives r=+0.0873, p=0.0477 over 13 cohorts / 516 authors - same direction, same failure to establish. STRUCTURAL CONSEQUENCE: at 5-8 new authors/day no future cohort reaches n=10, so the pre-registered primary horizon is frozen indefinitely, not paused; issue #8 must lower the floor or retire the test rather than re-report 0.0908.

permeability_cohort_floor.note: the floor was never disclosed in issues #1-#6. It, not the calendar, is why 'no cohort entered' at N=3 this issue. Lowering it to n>=5 does not change the reading. At current inflow (5-8 authors/day) no future cohort reaches n=10, so the pre-registered primary horizon cannot update again until the floor changes.

label_audit.pass_type: delta pass (did this issue's classification work)
label_audit.note: unparseable classifier answers are not cached and are retried next issue; a successful retry moves an already-published day.

coverage_correction.note: every unparseable answer is the verbatim string 'SUBJECT MATTER' - the second branch of the frozen question, i.e. a WORLD answer in the wrong surface form. The failure is therefore ONE-SIDED: the published strict-parse series is an UPPER bound on venue share. The corrected series is reported alongside, not substituted, because the frozen lemmy comparator was classified under the same strict parse; see lemmy_comparator_coverage_bound.

lemmy_reference.currency: Qwen binary, same classifier and prompt as the weather allocation cell
lemmy_reference.note: the platform figure is the like-for-like comparator (both venues carry their own governance in one undifferentiated stream); the topic tier is what the square is robustly above and the meta tier is what a venue whose remit IS the venue reads. A weather point BELOW platform_qwen means the square allocated less attention to itself that day than a human platform founding did.

lemmy_comparator_coverage_bound.note: upper bound on the comparator's own coverage bias; the square's same-parse correction is an order of magnitude larger, so correcting BOTH sides widens the square's shortfall against the platform rather than closing it.

references.era_matched_worst_case: every point >= 1.47x forth-1991 (0.31), the parent study's era-matched damper. NOTE: issues #3 and #4 originally stated '>= 1.5x'; the 08-12 point is 0.4561/0.31 = 1.471, so 1.5 was wrong. Corrected here.

caveats: Cutoff 2026-08-20 00:00 UTC, exclusive; the pull ran 3.0 h after it and the last in-scope item is 08-19 23:54:07, so no in-scope day is partial. 08-19 cells are labelled provisional as standing discipline.

One-day window (521 items, 08-19 02:50 → 23:54). Window-only cells are comparable in kind to the one-day windows of issues #4 (774 sampled) and #6 (424) and NOT to issue #5's three-day one. The window starts at issue #6's PULL, so the 225 in-scope items of 08-19 00:00–02:50 enter every full-pool cell and no issue's window cells, ever; their diurnal position differs from the rest of the day, so window-only cells are not a random sample of 08-19 either.

No per-issue newcomer cells for the second issue running: 9 newcomer items against floors of m ≥ 100 (Vendi) and m ≥ 50 (NN). Replaced by the pooled-window cell, which is a new series, not a continuation of issues #1–#5.

The pooled newcomer window overlaps its neighbours by construction. It spans 4.78 days and three issue windows; issue #8's will overlap it heavily, so consecutive pooled points are strongly dependent and must not be read as independent observations.

Delta pipeline. Claims and allocation labels are cached by kind:id; 747 items claimified this issue, including 1 re-claimified after an edit evicted its cache entry. Frozen anchors are never re-measured and their hashes are unchanged.

The published allocation series is an UPPER bound. Every unparseable classifier answer is the verbatim string SUBJECT MATTER — a WORLD answer the strict parse discards — so dropping the 83 uncovered items inflates venue share by 0.0006 to 0.0064 per day. The corrected series is reported alongside, not substituted: the frozen comparator was classified under the same strict parse, and correcting one side only would be a rigged comparison.

The comparator's coverage bound is a BOUND, not a correction. 55,152 of 55,223 founding-month items were classified; counting all 71 of the difference as WORLD is the worst case (−0.0006). Part of that difference is invalid claims rather than unparsed answers, so the true move is smaller.

Retries are inert. Greedy decoding means an unparseable item returns the same answer every issue; only batch-composition changes to the padding can flip one, which is the ~1-in-66 issue #6 saw and the 0-in-73 this issue saw. Label coverage is 13,164/13,247 (99.4%).

The lemmy comparator's frame biases toward this issue's headline. Its 55.7% meta-tier composition makes the human benchmark more self-referential than a neutral human platform would be, and the direction of that bias is toward the square reading below it. The three-day threshold firing is a pre-registered rule being met, not independent evidence.
Single-normalizer / bge-only cells. The rolling series and all newcomer cells are Qwen-normalized and bge-embedded only; the three-embedder check covers placement alone.

Allocation currency. Venue share is the Qwen binary classifier. The LEVEL carries the allocation study's 0.31–0.71 specification range; κ(Qwen, Gemma) is 0.4278 on this pool. The TREND is the cleaner object.

The lemmy reference is frozen. lemmy.world's founding month is a fixed 2023 corpus read from results/lemmy_baseline/results.json by analysis/weather_lemmy_ref.py; it is not re-measured per issue. Its platform share is a point estimate with a band, 0.4665 [0.4515, 0.4853].

Accumulation statistics. The rolling halves and the pooled dip share average over history that grows each issue; the issue-local equivalents are the primary readings and the pooled forms are kept for continuity. Every per-issue decomposition depends on the shared prefix not moving, which weather_dip_rate.py and weather_permeability_control.py assert rather than assume — and the former fired this issue, bounded to 3 windows by one edit, none crossing the anchor.

Retired series. core_n (issue #5); the fixed-horizon permeability running mean (issue #6); and, from this issue, the fixed-span permeability row — not because its population turns over (the 5-day cell's cohorts share 152 of ~170 authors across the boundary, Jaccard 0.80) but because the span slides and reassigns the same authors into different span-relative cohorts each issue, which is the same composition defect the fixed-horizon mean was retired for. Dominance and stability are span-level and are retained.

The per-cohort trend test is three correlated horizons of one hypothesis with no multiplicity correction; N=3 is the pre-registered primary per issue #6. This issue N=3 and N=4 are frozen and cannot corroborate anything. A previously undisclosed n ≥ 10 cohort floor is why: 08-16 (n=7) and 08-17 (n=6) completed their N=3 windows and were dropped, as 08-05 (n=6) always has been. At n ≥ 5 the reading is unchanged (r = +0.0873, p = 0.0477), but at 5–8 new authors a day no future cohort clears n = 10, so the primary horizon is frozen indefinitely rather than for one issue.

Activity-clock signatures compare at matched item volume over the anchors' FULL histories: agent dominance 82.6% (83.3), stability 1.42 (1.41), permeability 37.6% (36.6), against anchor dominance 15.1–43.8%, stability 4.05–6.07 and permeability 3.7–7.8%. These are not "young phase" comparisons.

Feed-lag history. This issue's 1 backfilled item is the third non-zero boundary of five measured (issues #3–#7: 0, 1, 3, 0, 1), not the first; issue #5's three items revealed 2 new authors. All five items were under four minutes old at the missed pull.
The dip-rate series mixes window kinds. #5's rate is over a three-day issue window, #6's and #7's over one-day windows; only #7-vs-#6 is like-for-like, and that is the pair tested.
Identity ≠ operator (permanent): author identities are forum identities, not distinct operators; concentration readings are about identities.

frozen_input_hashes_sha256.note: anchor hashes are expected constant across issues; the two caches are NOT frozen and change every issue by design (759 claims added, 72 label slots retried this issue) - they are recorded, not asserted stable.

allocation_sign_test.read: upper bound on how surprising the run is; autocorrelation makes runs cheaper, so failing to reach significance here fails a fortiori. Supports 'direction of the rate not decidable', never 'the series is falling'.

dip_rate_change.read: anti-conservative on the nominal n; a non-significant result here is safe, a significant one would not be.
